questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The speaker's tone was CONCILIATORY toward the protesters." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, conciliatory means aimed at winning over; hostile is the reverse. So "hostile" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "Farmers were ELATED when the rains finally arrived." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, elated means extremely happy, i.e. overjoyed. So "overjoyed" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The council gave a SWIFT reply to the complaint." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, swift means fast; the opposite is slow. So "slow" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "Her ABRUPT departure surprised everyone." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, abrupt means sudden and unexpected. So "sudden" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The festival turned a quiet town into a LIVELY place." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, lively means full of energy; the opposite is dull. So "dull" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The old professor was RENOWNED for his research." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, renowned means widely known and respected, i.e. famous. So "famous" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The new policy will ENHANCE the quality of schools." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, enhance means to raise or improve; diminish is to lessen. So "diminish" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The villagers were APPREHENSIVE about the coming cyclone." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, apprehensive means worried that something bad will happen. So "anxious" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The captain's decision was HASTY." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, hasty means done too quickly without thought; considered means thought through. So "considered" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The judge was LENIENT with the first-time offender." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, lenient means not severe in punishing, i.e. merciful. So "merciful" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The lecture was TEDIOUS for the audience." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, tedious means boring and tiresome; the opposite is interesting. So "interesting" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The comedian's wit was UNPARALLELED." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, unparalleled means having no equal, i.e. matchless. So "matchless" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The monk led a SECLUDED life in the Himalayas." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, secluded means kept away from others, i.e. isolated. So "isolated" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The CANDID remarks of the chairman surprised the board." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, candid means frank; evasive means avoiding a direct answer. So "evasive" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The audience was CAPTIVATED by her singing." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, captivated means held spellbound, i.e. enthralled. So "enthralled" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The athlete showed REMARKABLE stamina." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, remarkable means worthy of notice; ordinary is the reverse. So "ordinary" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The clerk was REPRIMANDED for coming late." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, reprimand means to scold formally, i.e. rebuke. So "rebuked" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The author's argument was COHERENT." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, coherent means logically connected; disjointed is not connected. So "disjointed" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The two cousins have a CORDIAL relationship." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, cordial means warm and friendly. So "friendly" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The speaker's mood was SOMBRE." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, sombre means dark and gloomy; cheerful is the reverse. So "cheerful" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The company's profits DWINDLED over the year." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, dwindle means to diminish gradually, i.e. decline. So "declined" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The bank will FORFEIT the deposit if the terms are violated." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, forfeit means to lose a right or property as a penalty. So "lose" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The professor's lecture was ABSTRUSE, and few students followed it." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, abstruse means hard to understand, i.e. obscure in meaning. So "obscure" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The witness's testimony was EVASIVE." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, evasive means avoiding directness; straightforward is direct. So "straightforward" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The committee decided to EXPEDITE the approval process." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, expedite means to speed up a process. So "hasten" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The CHAOTIC traffic of Mumbai calmed after midnight." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, chaotic means completely disordered; orderly is the opposite. So "orderly" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "His speech was full of PLATITUDES that everyone had heard before." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, platitude means a remark made stale by overuse, i.e. cliché. So "clichés" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The sudden rise in prices was TRANSIENT." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, transient means short-lived; permanent is lasting. So "permanent" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "She is known for her PERSPICACITY; she spots problems early." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, perspicacity means keen mental perception, i.e. insight. So "insight" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The monarch's rule was BENEVOLENT." Choose the antonym (word opposite in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, benevolent means kindly and well-meaning; cruel is the reverse. So "cruel" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The CURSORY inspection missed several defects." Choose the synonym (word closest in meaning) of the word in capitals as used here.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, cursory means hasty and not thorough, i.e. superficial. So "superficial" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: ARDENT
questions.explanation: Ardent: ardent means full of fervour, i.e. passionate. So "passionate" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: ADVERSITY
questions.explanation: Adversity: adversity means misfortune and difficulty, i.e. hardship. So "hardship" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: AFFLUENT
questions.explanation: Affluent: affluent means having abundant wealth. So "wealthy" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: ARDUOUS
questions.explanation: Arduous: arduous means requiring great effort, i.e. difficult. So "difficult" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: FEEBLE
questions.explanation: Feeble: feeble means lacking strength, i.e. weak. So "weak" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: FUTILE
questions.explanation: Futile: futile means incapable of producing any result, i.e. useless. So "useless" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: TRIVIAL
questions.explanation: Trivial: trivial means of little value or importance. So "unimportant" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: WARY
questions.explanation: Wary: wary means watchful about possible danger, i.e. cautious. So "cautious" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: SORROW
questions.explanation: Sorrow: sorrow means deep distress, i.e. grief. So "grief" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: INEVITABLE
questions.explanation: Inevitable: inevitable means certain to happen; avoidable can be prevented. So "avoidable" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: CONSPICUOUS
questions.explanation: Conspicuous: conspicuous means easily seen; hidden is the opposite. So "hidden" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: NOVICE
questions.explanation: Novice: novice means a beginner; expert is highly skilled. So "expert" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: OBSOLETE
questions.explanation: Obsolete: obsolete means out of date; modern is current. So "modern" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: TINY
questions.explanation: Tiny: tiny means extremely small; huge is extremely large. So "huge" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: ABUNDANCE
questions.explanation: Abundance: abundance means a large quantity; scarcity is shortage. So "scarcity" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: ALLEVIATE
questions.explanation: Alleviate: alleviate means to make suffering less severe, i.e. relieve. So "relieve" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: AUDACIOUS
questions.explanation: Audacious: audacious means willing to take bold risks, i.e. daring. So "daring" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: CAPRICIOUS
questions.explanation: Capricious: capricious means given to sudden changes of mood, i.e. fickle. So "fickle" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: CENSURE
questions.explanation: Censure: censure means to express strong disapproval, i.e. condemn. So "condemn" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: COHERENT
questions.explanation: Coherent: coherent means logical and consistent. So "logical" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: DIFFIDENT
questions.explanation: Diffident: diffident means lacking self-confidence, i.e. shy. So "shy" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: DUBIOUS
questions.explanation: Dubious: dubious means hesitating or doubting. So "doubtful" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: HAUGHTY
questions.explanation: Haughty: haughty means disdainfully proud, i.e. arrogant. So "arrogant" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: IMPEDE
questions.explanation: Impede: impede means to delay or hinder progress, i.e. hamper. So "hamper" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: LUCRATIVE
questions.explanation: Lucrative: lucrative means producing a great deal of profit. So "profitable" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: METICULOUS
questions.explanation: Meticulous: meticulous means showing great attention to detail, i.e. painstaking. So "painstaking" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: PLAUSIBLE
questions.explanation: Plausible: plausible means seeming reasonable, i.e. believable. So "believable" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: STEADFAST
questions.explanation: Steadfast: steadfast means firmly fixed and loyal, i.e. unwavering. So "unwavering" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: COMPLACENT
questions.explanation: Complacent: complacent means uncritically self-satisfied; concerned is alert and worried. So "concerned" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: DIFFIDENT
questions.explanation: Diffident: diffident means lacking confidence; confident is self-assured. So "confident" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: EXACERBATE
questions.explanation: Exacerbate: exacerbate means to make worse; soothe means to ease. So "soothe" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: FASTIDIOUS
questions.explanation: Fastidious: fastidious means very hard to please; easygoing is relaxed and undemanding. So "easygoing" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: GREGARIOUS
questions.explanation: Gregarious: gregarious means fond of company; solitary prefers being alone. So "solitary" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: IMPARTIAL
questions.explanation: Impartial: impartial means treating all sides equally; biased favours one side. So "biased" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: INNOCUOUS
questions.explanation: Innocuous: innocuous means not harmful; harmful is the opposite. So "harmful" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: INDIGENT
questions.explanation: Indigent: indigent means poor; affluent means wealthy. So "affluent" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: LETHARGY
questions.explanation: Lethargy: lethargy means a lack of energy; vigour is strong energy. So "vigour" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: PROLIFIC
questions.explanation: Prolific: prolific means producing much; unproductive produces little. So "unproductive" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: RAMPANT
questions.explanation: Rampant: rampant means spreading unchecked; controlled is held in check. So "controlled" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: SPORADIC
questions.explanation: Sporadic: sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals; continuous never stops. So "continuous" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: EXONERATE
questions.explanation: Exonerate: exonerate means to clear of blame, i.e. absolve. So "absolve" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: ERUDITE
questions.explanation: Erudite: erudite means having great learning, i.e. scholarly. So "scholarly" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: EXTOL
questions.explanation: Extol: extol means to praise enthusiastically, i.e. laud. So "laud" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: QUELL
questions.explanation: Quell: quell means to put an end to, usually by force, i.e. suppress. So "suppress" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: PANACEA
questions.explanation: Panacea: panacea means a remedy believed to cure every problem. So "a cure for all ills" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is closest in meaning (synonym) to the word: PRAGMATIC
questions.explanation: Pragmatic: pragmatic means dealing with things sensibly and realistically, i.e. practical. So "practical" is the synonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: VOLATILE
questions.explanation: Volatile: volatile means liable to change rapidly; stable stays steady. So "stable" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: PENURY
questions.explanation: Penury: penury means extreme poverty; affluence means abundant wealth. So "affluence" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: NONCHALANT
questions.explanation: Nonchalant: nonchalant means calm and unconcerned; anxious is worried. So "anxious" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to the word: ZENITH
questions.explanation: Zenith: zenith means the highest point; nadir is the lowest point. So "nadir" is the antonym.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The soldiers could [BEAR] the biting cold of Siachen without complaint." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Here bear means to put up with something unpleasant, i.e. endure. Carry, produce and deliver are other senses of bear that do not fit.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The sun will [SET] by six in the evening." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Set used of the sun means to sink below the horizon, i.e. go down. The other options are different senses of set.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The [FAIR] umpire gave every decision without favour." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Fair for an umpire means treating both sides equally, i.e. impartial. Pale and average are other senses of fair.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The [MATCH] between Chennai and Mumbai went to the last ball." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Match here is a sporting contest. Partner and equal are other senses; spark is not a sense of match here.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The captain will [ADDRESS] the team before the final." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Address used with an audience means to speak to them. The other options are different senses.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The driver paid a [FINE] for jumping the signal." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Fine as a noun here is a sum of money charged as punishment, i.e. a penalty.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The [TRUNK] of the old banyan tree was very thick." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Trunk of a tree is its main woody stem or stalk. The other options are other senses of trunk.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The shopkeeper will [CLOSE] the shop at nine." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Close used as a verb with a shop means to shut it. Near, miserly and intimate are adjective senses.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The [SPRING] in the village never dries up." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Spring here is a place where water flows from the ground, i.e. a natural water source.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The [LIGHT] bag was easy to carry." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Light in the sense of little weight has the opposite heavy. Dark is the opposite only of light as brightness.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "Meera gave the [RIGHT] answer to the question." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Right meaning correct has the opposite wrong. Left is the opposite only for direction.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "She is a [KIND] teacher who never raises her voice." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Kind meaning gentle and considerate has the opposite cruel.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The batter swung the [BAT] and hit a six." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Bat in cricket is the wooden club used to hit the ball.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "Please [WATCH] the baby while I cook." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Watch a child here means to keep an eye on and care for, i.e. look after.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The children sat on the [BANK] of the river and fished." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Bank of a river is the land alongside it, i.e. the shore.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The judge asked the witness to [PRODUCE] the document in court." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Produce in this legal context means to bring out and show, i.e. present.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The company will [FLOAT] its new shares next month." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: To float shares means to put them on sale for the first time, i.e. launch them.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The doctor was [FIRM] about the patient's diet." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Firm here describes a person who does not yield, i.e. resolute.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The goalkeeper managed to [SAVE] the penalty with his left hand." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Save in football means to stop a shot from scoring, i.e. block it.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "Rohit decided to [PITCH] his idea to the investors." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Pitch an idea means to present it persuasively, i.e. propose it.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The new rules will [BEAR] upon every employee of the firm." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Bear upon means to be relevant to or affect, i.e. apply to.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The students were asked to [DRAW] a conclusion from the passage." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Draw a conclusion means to derive it from the evidence.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The minister will [FIELD] questions from reporters after the meeting." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Field a question means to handle and answer it.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The old tree could not [STAND] the force of the storm." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Stand the force of something means to withstand it.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The singer's [PITCH] was perfect throughout the concert." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Pitch in music is the highness or lowness of a note, i.e. its tone level.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The new manager has a [SOUND] knowledge of accounts." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Sound here means reliable and well founded, i.e. thorough.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The old man's [PLAIN] speaking won him respect." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Plain speaking is honest and direct speech, i.e. frank.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The captain's century helped [BOLSTER] the team's confidence." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Bolster means to support and strengthen.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The manager's [PRAISE] pleased the whole team." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Praise is approval; its opposite is criticism.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "Strict laws will [CURB] illegal mining in the district." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Curb means to hold back or keep in check, i.e. restrain.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The shopkeeper offered a [GENEROUS] discount during Diwali." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Generous here means large in amount; its opposite is meagre, i.e. small and inadequate.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The minister gave an [EVASIVE] reply to the question." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Evasive means avoiding a direct answer, i.e. indirect.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The sea was [TURBULENT] on the day of the storm." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Turbulent means violently disturbed; its opposite is calm.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "Ravi's [TENACIOUS] pursuit of the goal finally paid off." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Tenacious means holding firmly to a purpose, i.e. persistent.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "Her [CONCISE] summary saved everybody's time." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Concise means brief but complete; its opposite is wordy.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The two companies decided to [MERGE] last year." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Merge means to join together into one, i.e. combine.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The company's profit [SURGED] in the third quarter." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Surge means to rise sharply; its opposite is to plunge, i.e. fall sharply.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The trainer will [HONE] his skills before the finals." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Hone means to refine and sharpen, in this case skills.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "He was [RELUCTANT] to sign the form without reading it." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling; its opposite is eager, i.e. willing.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The chief's speech [PLACATED] the angry shareholders." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Placate means to calm someone who is angry, i.e. pacify.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "His [CAUSTIC] remarks hurt the new employee." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Caustic remarks are sharply sarcastic or bitter, i.e. biting.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The [OPAQUE] policy puzzled the citizens." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Opaque here means not open or clear; its opposite is transparent.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The negotiators tried to [MOLLIFY] the angry union." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Mollify means to appease someone's anger, i.e. soothe.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The [LAUDABLE] effort deserved a reward." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Laudable means deserving praise; its opposite is blameworthy, i.e. deserving blame.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The new technology will [OBVIATE] the need for fresh loans." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Obviate means to remove a difficulty or need, i.e. eliminate.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The [AUSPICIOUS] start of the campaign pleased the party." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Auspicious means promising success; its opposite is ominous, i.e. promising trouble.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The speaker's [VERBOSE] style bored the listeners." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Verbose means using more words than needed, i.e. wordy.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The jury's [UNANIMOUS] verdict ended the trial." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Unanimous means with everyone agreeing; its opposite is divided.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The critic [LAMBASTED] the film in his Sunday column." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the synonym (same meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Lambast means to criticise harshly, i.e. condemn.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The two leaders had an [AMICABLE] meeting in Delhi." the bracketed word is used in a particular sense. Choose the antonym (opposite meaning) of the bracketed word that fits this context.
questions.explanation: Amicable means friendly; its opposite is hostile.
